known_disanalogies: Strong convergence of semigroups can hold in a gapless theory; convergence itself is not a positive-gap certificate.
A changing-Hilbert-space theorem does not automatically respect Yang-Mills gauge quotients, regulator-dependent null spaces or physical source sectors.
Fixed-regulator or strong-coupling spectral separation does not automatically survive the continuum/weak-coupling trajectory.
A valid local operator lemma does not construct a nontrivial four-dimensional continuum Yang-Mills measure.
cheapest_hostile_world: Take the regulator and continuum Hilbert spaces identical with J_n=I and T_n(t)=T(t)=exp(-tH), where H has spectrum accumulating at zero above the vacuum; dense-domain strong semigroup convergence is exact while no positive mass gap exists.
